newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen weaker for second day.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen weaker for second day.

text.p: Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures are likely to ease for a second day in a row on Thursday, traders said.

They said that even with short-covering by dealers to roll-over short positions to the September contract ahead of a benchmark shift, the June may see a resistance point at 124.00-124.10, then at 124.40.

Disappointment at Wednesday's limited rises had weakened sentiment, a brokerage house dealer said. "The market had expected the June to rise smoothly toward 124.50 on Wednesday, but it failed to do so. This worsened a chart outlook."
"Wednesday's intraday high of 124.40 is now a firm resistance point," he added.
Traders said they expected the June to move between 123.30 and 124.10 against Wednesday's 123.72 close. Expected firmness in Tokyo stocks is also negative for JGBs, they said.
"Fears of higher interest rates appear easily as long as the current firmness in stocks continues," said another brokerage house dealer.
"It is difficult to try the topside now."
Traders said the Ministry of Finance is expected to auction 1.5 trillion yen of three-month Treasury bills during the day.
